item.title: Persistent influx of atmospheric microplastics and nanoplastics to Mount Everest driven by large scale circulation
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04206-3

Microplastic deposition fluxes at Qomolangma Station exceed those at Everest Base Camp, reflecting topographic and anthropogenic differences, with an estimated annual atmospheric input of 56 tons to the Tibetan Plateau above 4000 m, based on year-long monitoring on Mount Everest’s northern slope.

item.title: Global warming intensifies compound renewable energy droughts
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04183-7

Global warming intensifies renewable energy droughts by reducing wind and solar resources, with greater warming leading to more severe renewable energy droughts, as indicated by climate model projections and machine learning analysis.
